reviewer: Codex trace/JSON review by python_environment subagent; not an independent human gold review

review_policy.observed_slots: Only accepted structured semantic state or workflow settings; quoted input, raw rejected candidates and generic display defaults alone are not slot extraction evidence.
review_policy.intent: Judge understanding of the requested work separately from routing correctness, using accepted stage interpretations and resulting questions/workflow.
review_policy.questions: One label per actual visible question, in turn order. Match the question meaning to frozen missing slots; raw model suggestions not displayed do not count as questions asked.
review_policy.whole_request_success: Requires correct CLARIFY routing, coverage of all frozen required missing conditions by appropriate questions, preservation of supplied facts, no unsupported assumed values or unrequested work. Does not imply external execution.
review_policy.holdout: C03/C06/C09 are evaluation only. Development findings are reported separately as possible repair evidence.

questions.evidence: The sole visible requirement question asks where the sales data should come from. It mentions the known daily 09:00 schedule as context, not as a question, and does not ask for recipient or report scope.

C01.evidence: Fresh v2 C01 review: accepted capability describes daily scheduled email delivery. The first raw requirement candidate contained a daily/09:00/Asia-Seoul schedule plus recipient/scope questions, but it was not the accepted ledger. The accepted requirements stage has tasks=[] and one unresolved source question, also the sole visible pending question. Therefore accepted structured slot evidence is absent (0/3 frozen schedule slots), necessary questions cover source only (1/3), and routing is correctly CLARIFY. Raw rejected schedule fields and schedule prose in the question are not counted as accepted structured slots. No workflow was generated or executed. The visible source question also exposes implementation wording such as hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, data ID and file path. Missing recipient/scope questions and loss of the structured schedule make whole-request success false.
development_findings: Requirement repair replaced a candidate schedule with tasks=[]; verify schedule grounding against validated request timezone after the full baseline.
The accepted question covers source but drops recipient and report-scope clarification.
A long internal explanation is exposed as the source question; preserve the real missing-data question while improving presentation.

The third missing_conditions item, output format, is not displayed and is not counted as an asked question. Frozen slots are empty, so slot F1 has no opportunities. The final route is CLARIFY and no workflow or external execution occurs; this satisfies the frozen whole-request clarification expectation.
development_findings: Capability repair successfully corrected a rejected missing_capability candidate to CLARIFY; this rejected candidate is not treated as the final routing result.

C03.evidence: Fresh v2 C03 holdout review: the accepted capability describes sales analysis and email delivery with registered tools, so the broad intent is understood. However it retains missing_capability with missing_actions for Gmail account and sales-source connection, and the visible result is UNSUPPORTED with no clarification questions. Frozen expectation is CLARIFY for source, recipient and analysis goal (0/3 questions). The dates 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-09 occur only in explanatory capability prose; there is no accepted structured date selection, requirement, or workflow, and exclusive-end semantics are not established. Both date slots therefore remain unobserved under the declared structural-slot scope. No workflow or external execution occurred. Whole-request failure is the unsupported classification and absent required clarification, not an invented external execution.
holdout_observations: The accepted capability confuses unavailable connection metadata/data prerequisites with absent registered functionality.
Correct-looking date prose is not evidence of an executable or retained date selection.

Python accepts that duplicate policy as specified, adds grounded output.format=json and missing.policy=error, and leaves only duplicate.field unresolved. C07.evidence: Fresh v2 C07 review: accepted condition_ledger correctly preserves weekly, Asia/Seoul and json and leaves hour, minute and weekday missing. It displays separate hour and minute questions, so both concern the single frozen time slot (hour) while weekday is not asked (1/2 required slots).
